title: Ecocriticism: reading literature for the living world
examples: How do I write an ecocritical reading of a poem?

explain.say: In 1879 Gerard Manley Hopkins found the poplar trees by a river near Oxford cut down, and wrote: All felled, felled, are all felled. You can hear the axe in the repeats. Ecocriticism asks how literature imagines nature, and our place in it. The board sorts its big ideas.

draw.text: Ecocriticism: reading literature for the living world

explain.say: First group: pastoral, the dream of a peaceful countryside, from ancient shepherd songs to Wordsworth's Lakes. Ecocritics love it and question it. Raymond Williams asked who did the farm work that the poems leave out. Whose labour is missing from a pretty landscape?

Next, wilderness and apocalypse. Henry David Thoreau lived in a cabin by Walden Pond, and nature became a teacher. Rachel Carson's Silent Spring, in 1962, opened with a fable of a town where the birds fell silent. How do stories of disaster change what people do?

Here is how the field grew. William Rueckert coined the word ecocriticism in 1978, Cheryll Glotfelty's collection launched it in 1996, and in 2016 the Indian novelist Amitav Ghosh asked why serious fiction has mostly ignored climate change. What would a climate novel set in your town look like?

explain.say: So ecocritics read for two things. On the left, nature as backdrop and property. On the right, nature as an actor, a living system. Well done. Exam tip: ask what the non-human does in the text, and who profits from the land. Challenge: reread a poem and give the landscape a voice.

faq.a: The study of literature and the environment: how texts represent nature, animals, land and climate, and how they shape the ways people treat the living world.
A tradition of writing that idealises rural life and shepherds, from Theocritus and Virgil to Wordsworth. Ecocritics study both its love of nature and what it hides.
asks: What does pastoral mean in literature?

faq.a: William Rueckert, in a 1978 essay called Literature and Ecology: An Experiment in Ecocriticism.
asks: Where does the word ecocriticism come from?

faq.q: What is The Great Derangement about?
faq.a: Amitav Ghosh's 2016 book asks why serious modern fiction has mostly avoided climate change, and argues this silence is part of a wider failure of imagination.

faq.q: How do I write an ecocritical reading?
faq.a: Notice how nature is presented: backdrop, resource or actor. Ask who owns and works the land, what happens to animals and places, and whether the text sees humans as part of nature.

facts: William Rueckert coined the word ecocriticism in 1978.
Rachel Carson's Silent Spring was published in 1962.
Hopkins wrote Binsey Poplars in 1879; it was published in 1918.
